transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my sleep has become completely unmoored lately. 

At first, it was... well, I was waking up after just two or three hours of sleep, and I'd be up drafting plans, feeling completely ready to go. But now, I just lie awake long before dawn. My stomach is tight, and I don't feel any sense of rest at all. It's just really taking a toll.
When you were sleeping only two or three hours, did you still feel rested and energized the next day?

Yes, exactly. It was... unusual. I would get maybe three hours of sleep, sometimes less, and I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed. Like I'd had a full eight hours. I didn't feel tired during the day at all. I actually felt like I had more energy than usual, which is why I was up doing so much. It just didn't make sense for someone my age to need so little sleep, but I felt fine... at least, back then I did.
How long did that period of sleeping very little while feeling rested and unusually energized last?

Well, it went on for about five months. It started right after a big investment loss I had. During that whole time, I wasn't really living like my usual retired self at all. Everything I did, all that energy... it just revolved around trying to undo the financial damage.
Did you need to be hospitalized because of what was happening during that period?

No, I wasn't hospitalized. I mean, I was definitely acting out of character and barely sleeping, but I wasn't... I didn't end up in the hospital or anything like that. I was just entirely focused on my finances at home.
During that five-month period, did your behavior cause major problems in your daily functioning or relationships?

Yes, it really did. Um... my wife has actually had to step in and take over all of our finances. And she basically has to stay with me at the house now, just for my own safety. 

As for my usual routine... well, I just stopped showing up for things. I'm usually very involved with the local museum and the arts council, but I haven't been reliable with any of that. I stopped seeing my friends, too. So, yes, it caused a major disruption to pretty much every part of my life.
During that five-month period, did you feel unusually euphoric or high in mood compared with your usual self?

Yes, I did. Um... for weeks during that time, I felt almost brilliantly optimistic. It was like every obstacle in my way was just trivial. I felt like I could fix everything. 

But at the same time... well, if anyone questioned my plans or tried to slow me down, I got incredibly angry. I snapped at them. I felt like they were trying to sabotage me, and I honestly believed I was the only sensible man in the room.
During that five-month period, were you using any intoxicating substances?
No, I wasn't. I mean, I don't use drugs, and I wasn't drinking heavily or anything like that. So, no, there weren't any substances involved. It was just... just me.
Have you ever had a distinct period of depression that required mental-health treatment?

No, I haven't. Um... I've never really dealt with a period of depression like that. Certainly nothing that ever required me to get mental-health treatment. So, no, it's really just been... well, the kind of things I was just describing to you.
